theory.overview: Network Flow deals with flow in directed graphs with capacities. Key problem: find maximum flow from source to sink. Applications: bipartite matching, transportation, scheduling, and image segmentation. Classic algorithms: Ford-Fulkerson (with BFS/DFS), Edmonds-Karp (BFS), Dinic's algorithm. This chapter covers max flow, min cut theorem, and flow algorithms.

sections.title: Flow Network
sections.content: Directed graph with source s, sink t, and edge capacities. Flow must satisfy: capacity constraint (flow ≤ capacity), flow conservation (flow in = flow out at all nodes except s and t). Max flow: maximum total flow from s to t. Min cut: minimum total capacity of edges separating s from t.
properties: Max flow = Min cut (Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem)

sections.title: Ford-Fulkerson Algorithm
sections.content: Repeatedly find augmenting paths (paths from s to t with available capacity) and augment flow. Residual graph: graph showing remaining capacity. When no augmenting path exists, flow is maximum. Time: $O(E \times f)$ where f is max flow (can be slow for large flows).
sections.algorithm: Find augmenting path in residual graph. Augment flow by bottleneck capacity. Update residual graph. Repeat until no augmenting path.

sections.title: Edmonds-Karp Algorithm
sections.content: Ford-Fulkerson with BFS to find shortest augmenting path (in edges). Guarantees $O(VE^2)$ time regardless of flow value. BFS ensures polynomial time. Practical for moderate-sized graphs.
sections.algorithm: BFS in residual graph to find shortest augmenting path. Augment flow. Repeat.

sections.title: Dinic's Algorithm
sections.content: More efficient max flow algorithm. Constructs level graph using BFS (layers from s). Uses DFS to send blocking flow (saturates at least one edge per DFS). Rebuilds level graph when no more augmenting paths. Time: $O(V^2E)$ or $O(E \sqrt{V})$ for bipartite matching.
sections.algorithm: BFS to build level graph. DFS to send blocking flow. Rebuild level graph when stuck. Repeat until t unreachable.

sections.title: Applications
sections.content: Bipartite matching: transform to max flow (source to left, right to sink, edges with capacity 1). Maximum bipartite matching = max flow. Image segmentation: source to foreground, background to sink, edge weights = similarity. Min cut = optimal segmentation. Project selection: profit/cost as flow/capacity.

keyConcepts.name: Residual Graph
keyConcepts.description: Graph showing remaining capacity on each edge. Forward edge: c - f. Backward edge: f (allows undoing flow).

keyConcepts.name: Augmenting Path
keyConcepts.description: Path from s to t in residual graph with available capacity. Bottleneck = min capacity on path.

keyConcepts.name: Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem
keyConcepts.description: Maximum flow equals minimum cut capacity. Cut: partition of vertices with s in one set, t in other. Cut capacity = sum of capacities crossing cut.

keyConcepts.name: Blocking Flow
keyConcepts.description: Flow that saturates at least one edge on every path from s to t in level graph. Dinic's uses blocking flows.

steps.title: Initialize
steps.description: Initialize flow to 0 on all edges. Build residual graph.
steps.code: flow = {e: 0 for e in edges}; residual = build_residual_graph();

steps.title: Find Augmenting Path
steps.description: Find path from s to t in residual graph with available capacity.

steps.title: Calculate Bottleneck
steps.description: Find minimum capacity on augmenting path.
steps.code: bottleneck = min(residual[e] for e in path);

steps.title: Augment Flow
steps.description: Add bottleneck to flow, update residual graph.
steps.code: for e in path: flow[e] += bottleneck; residual[e] -= bottleneck; residual[reverse(e)] += bottleneck;

steps.title: Repeat
steps.description: Repeat until no augmenting path exists. Return max flow.
steps.code: while path: augment(); path = find_path(); return total_flow;

snippets.title: Edmonds-Karp (BFS Ford-Fulkerson)
snippets.code:
from collections import deque

def edmonds_karp(graph, source, sink):
    n = len(graph)
    flow = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    max_flow = 0
    
    while True:
        # BFS to find augmenting path
        parent = [-1] * n
        parent[source] = source
        q = deque([source])
        
        while q and parent[sink] == -1:
            u = q.popleft()
            for v in range(n):
                if parent[v] == -1 and graph[u][v] - flow[u][v] > 0:
                    parent[v] = u
                    q.append(v)
        
        if parent[sink] == -1:
            break  # No augmenting path
        
        # Find bottleneck
        path_flow = float('inf')
        v = sink
        while v != source:
            u = parent[v]
            path_flow = min(path_flow, graph[u][v] - flow[u][v])
            v = u
        
        # Augment flow
        v = sink
        while v != source:
            u = parent[v]
            flow[u][v] += path_flow
            flow[v][u] -= path_flow
            v = u
        
        max_flow += path_flow
    
    return max_flow  # O(VE^2)

snippets.title: Bipartite Matching as Max Flow
snippets.code:
def max_bipartite_matching(graph, n_left, n_right):
    # Convert to flow network
    # Source -> left nodes (capacity 1)
    # Left -> right edges (capacity 1)
    # Right nodes -> sink (capacity 1)
    
    n = n_left + n_right + 2
    source, sink = 0, n - 1
    flow_graph = [[0] * n for _ in range(n)]
    
    # Source to left
    for i in range(n_left):
        flow_graph[source][i + 1] = 1
    
    # Left to right
    for u, v in graph:
        flow_graph[u + 1][v + n_left + 1] = 1
    
    # Right to sink
    for i in range(n_right):
        flow_graph[i + n_left + 1][sink] = 1
    
    return edmonds_karp(flow_graph, source, sink)
